Definition: from a primary (but obsolete) ἔργω (to work); toil (as an effort or occupation); by implication, an act:--deed, doing, labour, work.
BiblicalUsage: Érgon is work — the deed, the task, the thing done. Paul says we are God's workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works; James says faith without works is dead; and Jesus says the work of God is to believe in Him whom He sent. The word holds the whole question of what faith does.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe érgon settles the argument about faith and works: faith that does nothing is not faith, and works that do not come from faith are not God's work. I hold that the works God prepared for me are the ones I should be walking in today.
RelatedEvents: The Feeding of the Five Thousand; The Resurrection
